summary: Edge cookie scope truncation siphons pinned sessions to standby variant
description: Issue summary: Several BrightHealthAI tenants observed that requests pinned to a promoted model variant (explicit model pin) were being served intermittently from the standby/degraded variant during a canary window. Impact: user requests returned responses from a legacy model resulting in small but visible output drift (customer-facing). Observed during a staged weight shift after a canary increase. Environment: prod, us-east regional edge cluster, dedicated pool for BrightHealthAI. Impact window: 2025-11-02 22:10 - 2025-11-03 01:45 UTC. Immediate customer impact: incorrect predictions for ~0.7% of requests during the window and elevated token costs due to fallback paths hitting larger variant.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightHealthAI tenant on prod-us-east with explicit model pin header: x-rw-model: rw-instruct-3b@2025-11-01
2) Start 40 rps steady traffic with session cookie domain set to .brighthealthai.com and path=/api/v1/prompt
3) Trigger a canary weight increase from 5% to 25% for promoted variant (operation performed by Platform team),
4) Observe routing for sessions created during the weight shift and compare model hash in request logs versus pinned header
Expected: All pinned sessions continue to route to pinned variant. Actual: ~0.7% of sessions were served by standby variant and showed model hash mismatch and different token counts.
logs: edge-proxy[2025-11-03T00:12:18Z] WARN session-cookie truncated domain->.brighthealthai.co; cookie_path=/api/v1/prompt
router[2025-11-03T00:12:19Z] INFO request tenant=brighthealthai session=abc123 routed_to=standby-variant model_hash=92f1ab (expected 4b7d2c)
orchestrator[2025-11-03T00:12:19Z] DEBUG pin_lookup tenant=brighthealthai session_cookie=abc123 pin=rw-instruct-3b@2025-11-01 expired=false
serving-runtime[2025-11-03T00:12:19Z] INFO started-inference model=rw-llama-13b@2025-10-25 variant=standby batch_id=4521
investigation_notes: 11/03 02:00 - Initial triage: support reviewed request traces and confirmed model_hash mismatch for routed requests.

11/03 03:15 - Edge logs show cookie domain truncation events when cookie length exceeded 200 bytes; truncation appears correlated with custom cookie namespace used by customer (session metadata + feature flags encoded into cookie).

11/03 04:00 - Hypothesis: cookie truncation changed the cookie's 'path' or 'domain' attributes, causing edge-proxy to create a new session fingerprint and skip the pin-lookup fastpath, which allowed the orchestrator to apply canary routing rules and pick standby variant.
11/03 05:20 - Reproduced locally by setting cookie payload>220 bytes: edge-proxy bug #412 reproduces truncation and path rewrite behavior.

11/03 07:10 - Confirmed that when pin lookup fails but explicit model header is present, some components still prefer orchestrator-assigned variant if session fingerprint mismatch occurs during canary windows.

11/03 08:45 - Cross-team notes: edge team has an open PR to limit cookie attribute truncation and preserve path/domain attributes (PR #412). Serving/runtime team to add defensive check: prefer explicit model pin header if present (PR #2876).
resolution: Hotfixes deployed: 1) edge-proxy patch (pr 412) to avoid scope truncation and preserve cookie path/domain when payload exceeds threshold; 2) runtime guard (pr 2876) to treat explicit x-rw-model header as authoritative and bypass orchestrator variant assignment when pin verification succeeds. Deployed to prod-us-east at 2025-11-06 04:30 UTC. Mitigation provided: customers can set an explicit header x-rw-pin-assert: true to force pin check until hotfix lands. Follow-ups: expand cookie size validation in client SDK, add canary-window telemetry metric for pin bypass, and publish runbook changes.
comments: Support - Asha Patel (2025-11-03T02:30): Customer reported inconsistent outputs after we increased canary weight. Attached sample traces and token billing spike. Asked for triage priority.
SRE - Marco Ruiz (2025-11-03T03:05): Reproduced mismatch in staging by inflating cookie payload. Opening edge-proxy investigation and notifying Edge team.
Edge - Lin Zhao (2025-11-03T04:10): Found cookie serialization code that drops attributes when cookie size >200 bytes. Draft patch available in PR 412. Needs review and perf test.
Runtime - Priya Menon (2025-11-03T07:55): Adding defensive check: if x-rw-model header exists and session pin record matches, runtime should short-circuit orchestrator routing. Working on PR 2876.
Customer - BrightHealthAI (2025-11-03T09:20): Thanks for the quick response. We can temporarily reduce cookie payload but would prefer a server-side fix. Please advise safe mitigations.

Support - Asha Patel (2025-11-04T12:00): Temporary mitigation: set x-rw-pin-assert: true in client and reduce cookie payload below 180 bytes. We've shared these steps with BrightHealthAI and updated ticket.
SRE - Marco Ruiz (2025-11-06T05:10): Hotfixes deployed to prod-us-east. Monitoring shows fallback rate dropped to <0.01% for affected tenant. Closing customer-impacting window.
